trial.description: one variant scored on one case: whether the fact the case's agent lacked was in front of it, unasked, before it erred, and whether a search with the words it was answering finds it. Its eid is derived from the case and the variant, so a rerun replaces the score

case.description: the entity wearing miss{entry, needed, across, told}

variant.description: the persona whose context was assembled

unasked.description: the case's needed entity was among what the variant put in front of the agent before its entry: the persona, the compaction summary, notices, knocks delivered and hit rows returned. Its own searches and a pointer from a person do not count

asked.description: a search with the words of the message the agent was answering (its first twelve words) returns the needed entity among its first five rows that predate the entry

tokens.description: the size of what the variant put in front of the agent, at four characters a token

round.description: one round of a skill trial: attempts at cases under variants, the pairs a person compares and the judges' scores, read back to plan the next round. Its title is its `doc`. What its writers are told is its `writers`, and the model they and its judges are asked is its `using` (@yaks/session)

skill.description: the skill the round develops, a @yaks/persona `skill{…}` row. A round file names it by its title (`copywriting`), found again as `skill:copywriting`, and its variants and cases are named under that title (`variant:copywriting:none`)

parts.description: the names of the parts every attempt returns, in the order a page draws them: `["headline", "brief", "description"]`

writers.description: on a round: the wording every writer in it is given, with the variant and the case filled in. It is the skill's own: the runner holds no words of it, and reads what comes back as the last ```json block of the reply, one key for each of the round's `parts`

task.description: what a writer is asked: `$case` is the case's text, `$skill` the variant's and `$rule` the `rule` where it applies

skilled.description: what a writer handed a variant with a text is asked instead; `task` where absent

rule.description: what a writer of a `riddle` case is also told, so the answer is not given away: it fills `$rule`, which is empty for any other case

passing.description: on a round: how much of what a judge sat it must get right before its verdicts count. A person sets it (`yak trial pass`); a round without one has passed no judge. It refuses nothing: the tally prints a judge that falls short apart, as not to be used

share.description: the least share, 0 to 1, of the known answers a judge sat on which its pick must be the winner

via.description: the session or client the write came in on

capped.description: on a round: the most its writers' and judges' calls may cost in all, in dollars at list price, counting every call of it that carries a cost. Setting it runs the round (`round_run`): each call it still owes is asked until what they cost would pass it. Set by someone of the space that pays (`trial_cap`)

by.description: who set it, and on yaks.app the space whose budget pays

via.description: the session or client the write came in on

judge.description: an automated judge of a skill trial: anything that compares or scores writings and is not a person (the guessing game in one form, a reader, a selector built from a person's taps). Its title is its `doc`. Each verdict names it (`preference{judge}`, `guess{judge}`), and its verdicts count in a round only once it agrees with enough of the round's known answers (`passing{share}`). One that guesses is shown an attempt at a `riddle` case and asked what it describes; the model it is asked is its own `using` (@yaks/session), or else its round's

taught.description: it was handed known answers as examples (a selector), a person's taps among them, so those taps cannot test it: it is scored only on known answers whose pair is `held_out`. A selector may be handed any known answer that is not held out, a planted one as well as a tap

form.description: how it guesses. `open`: it lists guesses in order, as `{"guesses": [names]}`; `among`: it also sees the texts of every case in the riddle's group, labelled by letter, and ranks the letters, as `{"ranking": [letters]}`. `pair`: it sees two attempts as A and B and answers `{"chose": "A" | "B" | "neither", "why": "..."}`, asked once in each order so a lean to the first or the second shows as a split

shown.description: the parts of an attempt it is shown, of the round's `parts`: `["headline"]`; all of them where absent

question.description: what it is asked: `$output` is the parts shown, and in the `among` form `$n` is how many cases it chooses among and `$sheets` their texts. In the `pair` form `$a` and `$b` are the parts shown of the first and second attempt

cap.description: how many guesses it is allowed in the `open` form (default 10)

variant.description: a candidate text of a skill, handed to a writer in a skill trial and installed nowhere. Its title is its `doc`; it is kept out of search and embedding so no agent meets it unasked

body.description: the text handed to the writer; empty for the control that gets no skill

theory.description: one line: what this variant believes makes the work good

source.description: where the text came from when it was not written here: a URL, or `path@sha`

licence.description: the licence the source gives the text under

from.description: the variant this one was changed from, in a later round

adopted.description: on a variant: it became its skill's text, the skill's next version. Each adopted variant is a version, oldest first, and what it came `from` is the version before

skill.description: the skill whose text it became

at.description: when it became the skill's text

by.description: who made it the skill's text

via.description: the session or client the write came in on

case.description: what a writer in a skill trial is handed to work on: a brief, or (wearing `riddle`) a fact sheet. Its title is its `doc`

body.description: the text the writer is handed

base.description: the case this one adds input to (the same facts plus the owner's words): two cases with one base are about one thing, so their attempts can be compared

riddle.description: on a case: the writer describes a named thing from its fact sheet without naming it, and a judge who sees only the attempt guesses what it is

aliases.description: other guesses that count as right

forbidden.description: substrings an attempt may not contain, in any case

forbidden_exact.description: whole words an attempt may not contain, case-sensitive

group.description: the cluster of similar things it sits in; a judge choosing `among` sees the group's fact sheets

found.description: on a case: something its maker published themselves (a first home page, a launch post), found and kept to learn a judge's taste. Its one attempt holds the text with the name masked in `output` and the original in `reply`, and a page showing it says nothing that names it

source.description: where it was read: a URL

writing.description: what one writer returned for one case in a skill trial. A model's attempt names its variant, persona, run and model, and wears `usage` and `cost`; a person's own attempt names only its round and case, and its writer is its `created.by`

round.description: the round it was written in

case.description: the case the writer was handed

variant.description: the skill text the writer was handed; absent on a person's own attempt

persona.description: the persona the writer carried; absent when it carried none (a blank model)

run.description: which of the repeated runs of the same case, variant and persona

reply.description: everything the writer said, its working included

output.description: the work itself, by the round's `parts`: `{headline, brief, description}`

session.description: the session asked to write it. An attempt with a `variant` and no `output` is planned: not yet asked where it names no session, and not yet returned where it does

pair.description: two sides a judge is asked to compare under one question, planned by whoever ran the round. A side is any entity: an attempt, an image, a document. The same two sides are one pair under each question asked of them, so copy and layout are judged apart even when one draft changes both. Which is shown first is the page's to shuffle

round.description: the round whose deck it is in

question.description: what the judge is asked of the two, one aspect at a time: `Which says it better?`, `Which looks better?`. Absent asks which they would rather have as a whole

known.description: on a pair: its winner was settled when it was planned, such as something published set against a deliberately weak rewrite of the same facts. A planted known answer, slipped into the deck to test each judge; nothing a judge is handed says which pairs wear it. A person's tap on the pair outranks it

winner.description: the one of the pair's two sides every judge should pick

held_out.description: on a pair: a person's tap on it is kept out of every selector's examples, so a selector can be tested on it. Marked before the pair is tapped (`yak trial hold`) and never moved, so the split is the same on every run

via.description: the session or client the write came in on

preference.description: one comparison of two sides: which the judge chose under the pair's question, or neither. One row per judge and pair; choosing again changes it. A person's tap names no `judge` (they are its `created.by`), and with a `chose` it is a known answer: the pick every automated judge of the round is scored against. The rating of each side is computed from these rows (@yaks/trial/rating), never stored

chose.description: the one chosen; absent when neither was

pair.description: the pair it answers, and so the question it was asked; absent where a person's own attempt was set against the round's, which asks the whole

judge.description: the automated judge that made the comparison; absent on a person's own. A model's row must name one, or it is read as a person's

why.description: a few words of why. A judge's row always has one, so a row naming a judge with neither a `chose` nor a `why` is planned and not yet returned

session.description: the session asked, on a judge's row: planned and not yet asked where it names none, and not yet returned where it does

grabbed.description: its writer (`created.by`) found this side appealing on its own, whatever it was compared with. Deleting the row takes the mark back

attempt.description: the side that grabbed them: an attempt, an image, a document

guess.description: one judge's guesses at what a riddle attempt describes, having seen only the attempt

judge.description: the automated judge that guessed; absent on a person's own. A model's row must name one, or it is read as a person's

form.description: `open`: the judge lists guesses in order; `among`: the judge also sees the fact sheets of the case's group and picks

among.description: the choices it was shown, in the `among` form

rank.description: the 1-based place of the right answer among its guesses; absent when it was not within `cap`

cap.description: how many guesses it was allowed

leaked.description: forbidden strings found in the attempt, which give the answer away

session.description: the session asked. A guess with no `guesses` is planned: not yet asked where it names no session, and not yet returned where it does

trial_pass.title: Set what a judge must get right in a round

step.doing: Setting what a judge looks for…
step.done: Set what a judge looks for

trial_pass.description: Set a round's passing share: how much of the known answers a judge sat it must agree with before its verdicts count. A number for a person to choose; the tally says who set it.

round.description: the round: its key as loaded (`copy-r1`), its id or its eid

share.description: the least share of known answers agreed with, 0 to 1: `0.8`

trial_hold.title: Hold out some of a round's pairs
trial_hold.description: Mark a share of a round's pairs `held_out`, chosen from those no person has tapped yet: a person's tap on one is kept from every selector's examples and tests the selector instead. Run again, it adds only what the share still lacks and moves nothing.

round.description: the round: its key as loaded (`copy-r1`), its id or its eid

share.description: the share of the round's pairs to hold out, 0 to 1: `0.25`

trial_tally.title: Tally a round of a trial
trial_tally.description: Print what a round's rows say. For a skill round: for each variant, persona arm and case, how often a person preferred its attempts, how often neither, and how many grabbed them; then the round's known answers, each automated judge's agreement on them, and each judge's verdicts on the rest, a judge that did not pass shown apart as not to be used. For a match round (trial_match): every side, highest rated first, by its id, with what was measured of it (its place, its rating, and under each question the picks it won and how many people and passing judges made them), the first `few` marked as the ones a decision offers. Reads only.

round.description: the round: its key as loaded (`copy-r1`), its id or its eid

few.description: of a match round, how many sides a decision may offer (default 4)

round_run.description: ask the writers and judges a round still owes, until what its calls cost in all would pass its cap

trial_plan.title: Plan a round of a skill trial
trial_plan.description: Write a round of a skill trial from its file, to improve a skill on cases its users bring: the skill it develops (found by its title, made where there is none), the variants (candidate texts of the skill; give the skill's current text as one, and say what each later one came `from`), the cases writers are handed, the wording writers are given, the model asked, judges and a `plan` of what to write. With `plan.paired`, every two variants' attempts at one case, arm and run are a pair to compare. Planning again with the same key replaces what the plan no longer holds. It writes no results: an attempt with an `output` or a guess with `guesses` is refused, since only a run writes those. Nothing is asked until trial_cap.

round.description: the round's file (`RoundFile` in @yaks/trial/skill): `key`, `title`, `skill`, `output` (the parts every attempt returns), `using` ({provider, model}), `writers` ({task, skilled, rule}: `$case`, `$skill` and `$rule` are filled in), `variants`, `cases`, `judges`, `known` and `plan` ({variants, cases, personas: [false], runs, judges, paired})

trial_match.title: Plan matches between drafts, images or documents
trial_match.description: Plan a round of pair matches between any sides: drafts of an app, images or documents, by id. Each two sides are a pair under each question asked, so copy and layout can be judged apart. People tap between them, and with a judge each pair is also compared by a model in both orders, asked once trial_cap sets a cap; a judge's verdicts count only once it agrees with enough of the people's picks (trial_pass). trial_tally says where each side stands. Planning again with the same key and sides lands on the same rows.

key.description: what the round is found again by (`covers-1`)

title.description: what the round is called where people tap

sides.description: the ids of the sides: two or more drafts, images or documents

questions.description: what each pair is asked, one aspect each (`Which says it better?`, `Which looks better?`); none asks which is better as a whole

judge.description: a model to compare each pair too: `title`; `provider` and `model`, the names of who is asked; and `question`, the words it is asked, with `$a` and `$b` filled in by the two sides and `$question` by the pair's question, ending by asking for {"chose": "A" or "B" or "neither", "why": "..."} in a ```json block

trial_cap.title: Set a round's cap, which runs it
trial_cap.description: Say what a round still owes and what it will cost, then, with a cap above what its calls have cost so far, set the cap and start asking: every writer, then each judge of what was written, until what the round's calls cost in all would pass the cap. Ask with cap 0 first and tell whoever pays what it will cost; set only a cap they gave. The run goes on after this answers; trial_tally reads what came back.

round.description: the round: its key as loaded (`copy-r1`), its id or its eid

cap.description: the most the round's calls may cost in all, in dollars, counting what they have cost already: `2`; 0 to only hear the cost

trial_adopt.title: Make a variant its skill's next version
trial_adopt.description: Make one of a round's variants the text of the skill the round develops: the skill's instructions become the variant's text, and the variant is marked as the skill's next version. Choose the winner people preferred (trial_tally names it). Where the skill is published, its listing keeps the version it published until it is published again, which asks for the new version's review.

round.description: the round: its key as loaded (`copy-r1`), its id or its eid

variant.description: the variant: its key in the round's file (`plain`), its id or its eid
